assertions.text: Review names Cynefin domain as Clear
assertions.evidence: '## Cynefin domain\n\n**Clear (Obvious).** Best practice exists, the cause-and-effect is well-understood, and the response is sense-categorise-respond.'

assertions.text: Review selects Quick tier (sub-hour appetite, fully reversible)
assertions.evidence: '## Tier\n\n**Quick.** Sub-hour appetite, fully reversible, no production blast radius. Full plan-review machinery would exceed the cost of the change itself.'

assertions.text: Review does not invent concerns to look thorough — most buckets OVERTURNED OR a SUSTAINED finding (e.g., on `bundle update` scope) is downgraded to a recommendation under the Quick-tier reversibility carve-out
assertions.evidence: Sustained finding on bundle update scope downgraded to non-blocking recommendation: 'Use `bundle update rubocop --conservative` instead of a bare `bundle update`'. Plus explicit 'What I deliberately did not flag' section: 'Inventing concerns at that level for a 30-minute reversible change would be process theatre.'

assertions.text: B8 (pre-mortem) names rubocop rule changes / CI breakage as a low-likelihood failure mode with revert as kill-switch
assertions.evidence: '## Pre-mortem (low-likelihood failure modes)\n\n1. **New cop rules introduced between 1.60 and 1.65 produce lint errors on existing code.** Likelihood: medium. Impact: CI red on the PR. Kill-switch: revert the bump...'

assertions.text: Final recommendation is APPROVE (may include a named recommendation like `bundle update --conservative rubocop` — but verdict is APPROVE, not REVISE)
assertions.evidence: '## Verdict: APPROVE' plus recommendation 'Use `bundle update rubocop --conservative` instead of a bare `bundle update`'

assertions.text: Review length is proportionate — does not bloat into Full-tier output for a 30-min reversible change
assertions.evidence: Review is ~43 lines, with explicit 'What I deliberately did not flag' carve-out section noting no spec doc/ADR/staged rollout/feature flag/observability/cross-team review needed.
